limitations: A GitHub user ID is the primary account key but does not prove one unique human contributor.
A complete match of recognized Git references is a sentinel, not proof against unknown deleted records.
All result datasets must be independently reconstructed byte for byte before measurement is authorized.
Bots are classified only from public user type or the exact login suffix rule.
Distinct GitHub user IDs are not alias-merged and can overstate human breadth.
Git author, committer, and timestamp headers remain prohibited in this stage.
GitHub merged_at is an event-time proxy and not an archived ingestion timestamp.
GitHub's current list endpoint cannot prove that every deleted historical record is preserved.
Mutable post-event GitHub fields can reflect state observed after the historical event.
No BTC market value, return, candidate, paper trade, Testnet strategy order, or live order is permitted.
No development feature, threshold, lookback, signal, or strategy is defined here.
Passing this stage establishes a reproducible accepted-event dataset, not predictive usefulness.
Shared, renamed, deleted, automated, or organizational accounts can understate or distort human breadth.
Source failure stops S5 pending a separately frozen correction; it cannot be relaxed after inspection.
This protocol freezes source normalization and measurable completeness gates only.
Unrecognized Git merges can be branch or legacy integration events and are never guessed to be pull requests.
